At mtrr_lookup_fixed_next(), when the condition
'if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))' becomes true,
mtrr_lookup_var_start() is called with iter->range with gargabe values from the
fixed MTRR union field. Then, list_prepare_entry() do not call list_entry()
initialization, keeping a garbage pointer in iter->range which is accessed in
the following __mtrr_lookup_var_next() call.

Fixes: f571c0973e4b8c888e049b6842e4b4f93b5c609c
Signed-off-by: Alexis Dambricourt <alexis@blade-group.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c b/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
index c146f3c262c3..0149ac59c273 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
@@ -539,6 +539,7 @@ static void mtrr_lookup_var_start(struct mtrr_iter *iter)
 
 	iter->fixed = false;
 	iter->start_max = iter->start;
+	iter->range = NULL;
 	iter->range = list_prepare_entry(iter->range, &mtrr_state->head, node);
 
 	__mtrr_lookup_var_next(iter);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c`**
   - A new line was added to initialize `iter->range` to `NULL` before it is assigned a value using `list_prepare_entry()`. This change ensures that `iter->range` does not contain garbage values when `mtrr_lookup_var_start()` is called.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c` addresses a bug that could lead to a kernel page fault due to uninitialized memory. By initializing `iter->range` to `NULL`, the patch prevents the subsequent call to `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` from accessing a garbage pointer, thereby ensuring that the function operates on valid data. This change is crucial for maintaining the consistency and stability of the memory type range registers (MTRR) handling in the KVM module.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs when the condition `if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges)` becomes true, leading to a call to `mtrr_lookup_var_start()` with `iter->range` containing garbage values. This results in `list_prepare_entry()` not properly initializing `iter->range`, which is then accessed in the subsequent `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` call, causing a kernel page fault due to dereferencing an invalid pointer.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtrr_lookup_var_start(struct mtrr_iter *iter)
 {
 	struct kvm_mtrr *mtrr_state = iter->mtrr_state;
 
 	iter->fixed = false;
 	iter->start_max = iter->start;
+	iter->range = NULL;
 	iter->range = list_prepare_entry(iter->range, &mtrr_state->head, node);
 
 	__mtrr_lookup_var_next(iter);
 }
